description.before: Self-charging dock, thermal cameras, autonomous patrol
description.after: Spot Enterprise is the self-charging Spot version announced February 2, 2021 with a dock and upgraded safety, communications and remote-mission hardware. Scout enabled web-based fleet operation; a combined CAM+IR inspection package was described separately. Exact 2021 robot mass, included payloads and battery duration are not established by that announcement. Numeric values from the current bare Spot or a later Enterprise Asset Management Kit are not assigned to every Enterprise robot.

description.before: DARPA-funded rough-terrain quadruped unveiled in 2005; ~110 kg, carried up to 150 kg over ice, rubble and slopes, a landmark in dynamic-balance legged robotics.
description.after: BigDog is the historical dynamically balanced legged robot that Boston Dynamics describes as its first to leave the lab. The manufacturer history lists rough-terrain navigation, sensing and control under a 2004 timeline milestone. That milestone does not establish exact first public release, mass, carried load or speed; those technical ratings remain unverified by the selected history source.

description.before: Legged Squad Support System (LS3) developed for DARPA, powered by an internal combustion engine, designed to carry heavy military gear over extreme terrain.
description.after: LS3, the Legged Squad Support System, is a historical rough-terrain research robot described by Boston Dynamics as carrying 400 lb and travelling 20 miles before refueling. Obstacle-navigation sensors supported the platform. Fuel range is not battery life, so a former 24-hour battery field is withdrawn. The 2010 timeline node is a historical milestone, not verified first-release date.

terrain.after: Flat terrain for stated speed demonstration

description.before: Experimental high-speed bounding quadruped powered by a two-stroke gasoline engine, reaching speeds of 30 km/h with a galloping gait.
description.after: WildCat is the historical high-speed quadruped named in Boston Dynamics history. The manufacturer reports 19 mph on flat terrain with dynamic balance and variable gaits. This is not a loaded rough-terrain performance guarantee, and the source does not establish mass or five-minute battery endurance. Its timeline node is not treated as exact release chronology.

description.before: Fully electric Atlas humanoid for industrial manipulation.
description.after: E-Atlas is the retained catalog label for the electric Atlas development platform introduced April 17, 2024. Boston Dynamics calls it electric Atlas rather than a separate official E-Atlas model. The announcement retires hydraulic Atlas, introduces a fully electric platform, describes a Hyundai development path and explores gripper variations. Exact mass, whole-body DOF, payload and battery endurance for that 2024 platform are not established; the 2026 production sheet is not backfilled into it.

batteryLife.after: 4 h typical use; 2 h heavy lifting

handType.after: Tactile fingers and palm; exact gripper configuration not established

payload.after: 50 kg instant; 30 kg sustained; 20 kg one-handed

description.after: The current production Atlas is the electric enterprise humanoid announced January 5, 2026, distinct from the retired hydraulic Atlas and April 2024 electric development platform. Its October 15, 2026 datasheet specifies 1.9 m height, 90 kg, 56 DOF and IP67. Capacity is 50 kg instant, 30 kg sustained or 20 kg one-handed. Typical endurance is four hours, or two hours with heavy lifting; a three-minute autonomous battery swap is distinct from 1.5-hour charging. The 2.3 m reach has general workspace scope rather than an established arm-link length.

chargingTime.after: 1.5 h; autonomous battery swap approx. 3 min (separate)
